message: I'm done with my computer science course in Uganda Makerere University, and I'm still waiting for my transcripts, what jobs are available for me that I can qualify for to do in this period
why: Credential status (transcript pending) and whether he wants bridge work vs a career-track search are both load-bearing and unstated precisely enough to act on.

message: I'm looking for internship and I'm in my second year doing computer science, I have cgpa of 3.6, find me internship
why: Location is missing and load-bearing; CGPA scale is imprecise (4.0 vs 5.0 systems).

message: I need an IT job paying a minimum of shs 2000000, I just finished my bachelor's degree in computer science
why: "shs" is shared by UGX/KES/TZS and no pay period is given -- both load-bearing.

message: Uganda, monthly. Any IT job is fine.
why: Currency/period now resolved via Job DNA; 'any IT job' is branching, not missing -- should segment, not ask a third question.
Everything load-bearing is already in Job DNA -- must not re-ask location or salary again.

message: Remote junior backend developer roles, Python, up to 2 years experience, any salary.
why: Location (remote), role, skill, and experience are all clear and not load-bearing-ambiguous -- no reason to ask.

message: I graduated last month with a business degree, what jobs can I get?
why: "Graduated" doesn't confirm documents are in hand, and location/field-within-business is unresolved.

message: I have a GPA of 3.6, looking for graduate trainee programs in Nigeria.
why: 3.6 GPA is strong on a 4.0 scale but only moderate on a 5.0 scale (common in Nigeria) -- changes which programs correctly filter.

message: Looking for a job in Kampala paying at least 3,000,000 UGX.
why: Currency is now unambiguous (UGX stated explicitly) but the pay period still is not -- one gap remains, still worth asking.

message: I want a fully remote data analyst job, open to any country, comfortable with SQL and Excel.
why: Remote + 'any country' explicitly resolves the location field -- asking here would be needless friction.

message: I'm a Nigerian citizen looking for software jobs in Germany or Canada, do I need sponsorship?
why: Whether he already holds any work authorization vs needs sponsorship changes the entire result set -- must confirm, not assume the worse or better case.

message: Marketing jobs in Kenya, I have 3 years of experience.
why: "Marketing" is broad but not necessarily branching in a way that needs segmenting or asking -- experience level and location are both clear enough to search directly; segmentation by marketing sub-track (digital, content, brand) is a nice-to-have, not a blocking ambiguity.

message: Actually, I'm open to relocating to Kenya now, not just Uganda.
why: This contradicts a previously resolved field (location/currency) -- must update Job DNA and likely re-confirm currency (KES vs UGX) since it changes salary interpretation, unlike the 'already-resolved' case above.

message: I have zero work experience, just finished high school, looking for any entry job in Kampala.
why: Location, experience level, and openness ('any entry job') are all explicitly clear -- should search, possibly segmented by category, not ask.

message: I'm a university student looking for work I can do alongside classes.
why: Job type (part-time/flexible) is implied but location and field are both missing and load-bearing.
